lesson.title: Two New Letters: ਸ and ਹ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday we met three special letters that carry vowel sounds: ੳ, ਅ, ੲ. Today we meet the next two letters in the Gurmukhi alphabet: ਸ (sassa) and ਹ (haha).

ਸ (sassa) makes a hissing sound, like the English 's'. ਹ (haha) makes a breathy sound, like the English 'h'. Say each name slowly: sass-aa... ha-haa. Notice how ਸ has a curl at the top, and ਹ has a tall straight line with a loop at the bottom.
You now know five Gurmukhi letters: ੳ, ਅ, ੲ, ਸ, ਹ. Keep practicing their names — tomorrow we'll add three more!

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਸ (sassa) and ਹ (haha)
Review the previous lesson's three vowel-bearer letters (ੳ, ਅ, ੲ) alongside the two new letters
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Quickly review yesterday's three letters (ੳ, ਅ, ੲ) — can the child name all three?
2. Introduce ਸ and ਹ one at a time, saying each name aloud together three times.
3. Ask the child to describe each letter's shape in their own words.
4. Trace each letter in the air before picking up a pencil.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more on the practice line.
6. Close by saying all five letters learned so far, in order: ura, aira, iri, sassa, haha.
differentiationTips: Struggling: review only the two new letters today, without requiring perfect recall of yesterday's three
Ready for more: ask the child to find a word starting with the 's' or 'h' sound in English, and compare the sounds
For a child who already recognizes the letters, have them write both from memory before tracing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: ਸ and ਹ are the next two letters in the traditional Painti Akhari sequence used by Gurmukhi primers, continuing directly from the vowel-bearer letters introduced in the previous lesson.
